title: GCM oversized AAD returns BUFFER_E (not silent skip) — defend this
description: Why correct: if AAD exceeds CRYPTO2DEV_AAD_MAXLEN (256 bytes) and the port silently skipped the SET_AAD ioctl, the device would authenticate with empty AAD instead of the provided one — an authentication bypass. Any subsequent decrypt with the correct AAD would fail, but the ciphertext+tag pair would still be accepted by an attacker feeding it with empty AAD. Returning BUFFER_E makes the encrypt fail hard. The oversized-AAD rejection test (test_aesgcm_oversized_aad) covers this. What a contributor might change: 'silently truncating AAD is better than failing.' It is not — authentication with wrong AAD is worse than a hard error.
